sanskrit: evam uktas tu savrīḍaṃ tūṣṇīṃ kiṃ cid avāṅmukhaḥ jagāma rājā duḥkhārto gaṅgādvārāya bhārata
english: Thus addressed, O Bharata, the king went away in shame, silent, his face slightly downcast, grieved, toward the Gate of the Ganges.

sanskrit: sa devaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatvā virūpākṣam umāpatim tapaś cacāra vipulaṃ tasya prīto vṛṣadhvajaḥ
english: Going for refuge to the god Virūpākṣa, the lord of Umā, he performed intense austerities; and Vṛṣadhvaja (Śiva) was pleased with him.

sanskrit: baliṃ svayaṃ pratyagṛhṇāt prīyamāṇas trilocanaḥ varaṃ cāsmai dadau devaḥ sa ca jagrāha tac chṛṇu
english: The three-eyed god himself, well pleased, received his oblation and granted him a boon; hear what he chose.

sanskrit: samastān sarathān pañca jayeyaṃ yudhi pāṇḍavān iti rājābravīd devaṃ neti devas tam abravīt
english: "May I conquer in battle all five Pāṇḍavas along with their chariots" — so the king said to the god; but the god replied, "No."

sanskrit: ajayyāṃś cāpy avadhyāṃś ca vārayiṣyasi tān yudhi ṛte 'rjunaṃ mahābāhuṃ devair api durāsadam
english: "You will be able to check them in battle — those who are unconquerable and unslayable — all except the mighty-armed Arjuna, who is difficult to approach even by the gods."

sanskrit: yam āhur ajitaṃ devaṃ śaṅkhacakragadādharam pradhānaḥ so 'straviduṣāṃ tena kṛṣṇena rakṣyate
english: "He whom they call the unvanquished god who bears conch, discus, and mace — that foremost among weapon-masters, Kṛṣṇa, protects him."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu nṛpatiḥ svam eva bhavanaṃ yayau pāṇḍavāś ca vane tasmin nyavasan kāmyake tadā
english: Thus addressed, the king returned to his own abode, while the Pāṇḍavas continued to dwell in the Kāmyaka forest.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca evaṃ hṛtāyāṃ kṛṣṇāyāṃ prāpya kleśam anuttamam ata ūrdhvaṃ naravyāghrāḥ kim akurvata pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Janamejaya said: After Kṛṣṇā (Draupadī) had been abducted and the greatest distress had been suffered, what did those tiger-men, the Pāṇḍavas, do thereafter?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ kṛṣṇāṃ mokṣayitvā vinirjitya jayadratham āsāṃ cakre munigaṇair dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having thus freed Kṛṣṇā and thoroughly defeated Jayadratha, Dharmarāja Yudhiṣṭhira sat in the company of the hosts of sages.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ madhye maharṣīṇāṃ śṛṇvatām anuśocatām mārkaṇḍeyam idaṃ vākyam abravīt pāṇḍunandanaḥ
english: In the midst of those great sages who were listening and lamenting with him, the son of Pāṇḍu spoke these words to Mārkaṇḍeya.

sanskrit: manye kālaś ca balavān daivaṃ ca vidhinirmitam bhavitavyaṃ ca bhūtānāṃ yasya nāsti vyatikramaḥ
english: "I believe that Time is mighty, and so is Fate ordained by providence — and the inevitable destiny of beings which none can transgress.

sanskrit: kathaṃ hi patnīm asmākaṃ dharmajñāṃ dharmacāriṇīm saṃspṛśed īdṛśo bhāvaḥ śuciṃ stainyam ivānṛtam
english: "For how could such a calamity touch our wife, who knows and practises dharma, who is pure — like theft touching what is false?

sanskrit: na hi pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ kiṃ cit karma vā ninditaṃ kva cit draupadyā brāhmaṇeṣv eva dharmaḥ sucarito mahān
english: "For Draupadī has never done any sinful act or blameworthy deed anywhere; on the contrary, she has always observed great dharma toward the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: tāṃ jahāra balād rājā mūḍhabuddhir jayadrathaḥ tasyāḥ saṃharaṇāt prāptaḥ śirasaḥ keśavāpanam parājayaṃ ca saṃgrāme sasahāyaḥ samāptavān
english: "Yet the dull-witted king Jayadratha abducted her by force; for that abduction he received the shaving of his head, and along with his allies he was fully defeated in battle.

sanskrit: pratyāhṛtā tathāsmābhir hatvā tat saindhavaṃ balam tad dāraharaṇaṃ prāptam asmābhir avitarkitam
english: "She has been recovered by us after slaughtering that Saindhava army, yet this abduction of our wife was something we never anticipated.

sanskrit: duḥkhaś cāyaṃ vane vāso mṛgayāyāṃ ca jīvikā hiṃsā ca mṛgajātīnāṃ vanaukobhir vanaukasām jñātibhir vipravāsaś ca mithyā vyavasitair ayam
english: "Painful is this forest life, and our livelihood through hunting; painful is the killing of animals by those who dwell in the forest among other forest dwellers; and painful is this banishment from our kinsmen through the machinations of the wicked.

sanskrit: asti nūnaṃ mayā kaś cid alpabhāgyataro naraḥ bhavatā dṛṣṭapūrvo vā śrutapūrvo 'pi vā bhavet
english: "Surely there must be some man more unfortunate than I — have you, venerable one, ever seen or heard of such a one?"

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca prāptam apratimaṃ duḥkhaṃ rāmeṇa bharatarṣabha rakṣasā jānakī tasya hṛtā bhāryā balīyasā
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: O bull of the Bharatas, Rāma suffered incomparable sorrow — his wife Jānakī was carried off by a mighty demon.

sanskrit: āśramād rākṣasendreṇa rāvaṇena vihāyasā māyām āsthāya tarasā hatvā gṛdhraṃ jaṭāyuṣam
english: From his hermitage, the lord of rākṣasas, Rāvaṇa, taking to the sky and resorting to magic, swiftly killed the vulture Jaṭāyus and carried her away.

sanskrit: pratyājahāra tāṃ rāmaḥ sugrīvabalam āśritaḥ baddhvā setuṃ samudrasya dagdhvā laṅkāṃ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Rāma recovered her, relying on the forces of Sugrīva, building a bridge across the ocean and burning Laṅkā with his sharp arrows.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kasmin rāmaḥ kule jātaḥ kiṃvīryaḥ kiṃparākramaḥ rāvaṇaḥ kasya vā putraḥ kiṃ vairaṃ tasya tena ha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: In what lineage was Rāma born? What was his prowess, what his valour? Whose son was Rāvaṇa? And what was the enmity between them?

sanskrit: etan me bhagavan sarvaṃ samyag ākhyātum arhasi śrotum icchāmi caritaṃ rāmasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ
english: All this, O venerable one, you should narrate to me properly; I wish to hear the story of Rāma of untiring deeds.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ajo nāmābhavad rājā mahān ikṣvākuvaṃśajaḥ tasya putro daśarathaḥ śaśvat svādhyāyavāñ śuciḥ
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: There was a great king named Aja, born in the lineage of Ikṣvāku; his son was Daśaratha, ever devoted to sacred study and pure of conduct.

sanskrit: abhavaṃs tasya catvāraḥ putrā dharmārthakovidāḥ rāmalakṣmaṇaśatrughnā bharataś ca mahābalaḥ
english: He had four sons skilled in dharma and statecraft: Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, Śatrughna, and the mighty Bharata.

sanskrit: rāmasya mātā kausalyā kaikeyī bharatasya tu sutau lakṣmaṇaśatrughnau sumitrāyāḥ paraṃtapau
english: Kausalyā was Rāma's mother; Kaikeyī was Bharata's; the two scorchers of foes, Lakṣmaṇa and Śatrughna, were sons of Sumitrā.

sanskrit: videharājo janakaḥ sītā tasyātmajā vibho yāṃ cakāra svayaṃ tvaṣṭā rāmasya mahiṣīṃ priyām
english: Janaka was king of Videha; Sītā was his daughter, O lord — whom Tvaṣṭṛ himself fashioned as the beloved queen of Rāma.

sanskrit: etad rāmasya te janma sītāyāś ca prakīrtitam rāvaṇasyāpi te janma vyākhyāsyāmi janeśvara
english: Thus the birth of Rāma and of Sītā has been related to you; now I shall also explain the birth of Rāvaṇa, O lord of men.

sanskrit: pitāmaho rāvaṇasya sākṣād devaḥ prajāpatiḥ svayaṃbhūḥ sarvalokānāṃ prabhuḥ sraṣṭā mahātapāḥ
english: Rāvaṇa's grandfather was no less than the god Prajāpati, the Self-existent, lord and creator of all the worlds, of great austerity.

sanskrit: pulastyo nāma tasyāsīn mānaso dayitaḥ sutaḥ tasya vaiśravaṇo nāma gavi putro 'bhavat prabhuḥ
english: Pulastya by name was his beloved mind-born son; Pulastya had a son named Vaiśravaṇa, born of a cow, who became a lord.

sanskrit: pitaraṃ sa samutsṛjya pitāmaham upasthitaḥ tasya kopāt pitā rājan sasarjātmānam ātmanā
english: He abandoned his father and attended upon his grandfather; in anger at this, his father, O king, created another self from himself.

sanskrit: sa jajñe viśravā nāma tasyātmārdhena vai dvijaḥ pratīkārāya sakrodhas tato vaiśravaṇasya vai
english: That one was born as the twice-born Viśravā, made from half of himself, wrathful, as a countermeasure against Vaiśravaṇa.

sanskrit: pitāmahas tu prītātmā dadau vaiśravaṇasya ha amaratvaṃ dhaneśatvaṃ lokapālatvam eva ca
english: But the grandfather, pleased in heart, granted Vaiśravaṇa immortality, lordship of wealth, and the rank of world-guardian.

sanskrit: īśānena tathā sakhyaṃ putraṃ ca nalakūbaram rājadhānīniveśaṃ ca laṅkāṃ rakṣogaṇānvitām
english: And also friendship with Īśāna (Śiva), a son named Nalakūbara, and the city of Laṅkā, filled with hosts of rākṣasas, as his capital.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca pulastyasya tu yaḥ krodhād ardhadeho 'bhavan muniḥ viśravā nāma sakrodhaḥ sa vaiśravaṇam aikṣata
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: The sage who had been born as a half-body from Pulastya's wrath — that wrathful one named Viśravā — he looked upon Vaiśravaṇa.

sanskrit: bubudhe taṃ tu sakrodhaṃ pitaraṃ rākṣaseśvaraḥ kuberas tatprasādārthaṃ yatate sma sadā nṛpa
english: The lord of rākṣasas, Kubera, recognized his father as wrathful, O king, and ever strove to propitiate him.

sanskrit: sa rājarājo laṅkāyāṃ nivasan naravāhanaḥ rākṣasīḥ pradadau tisraḥ pitur vai paricārikāḥ
english: That king of kings, Naravāhana (Kubera), dwelling in Laṅkā, gave three rākṣasī women to his father as attendants.

sanskrit: tās tadā taṃ mahātmānaṃ saṃtoṣayitum udyatāḥ ṛṣiṃ bharataśārdūla nṛttagītaviśāradāḥ
english: Those women, skilled in song and dance, then strove to please that great-souled sage, O tiger of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: puṣpotkaṭā ca rākā ca mālinī ca viśāṃ pate anyonyaspardhayā rājañ śreyaskāmāḥ sumadhyamāḥ
english: Puṣpotkaṭā and Rākā and Mālinī — O lord of men, O king — those slender-waisted ones, eager for the best, vied with one another.

sanskrit: tāsāṃ sa bhagavāṃs tuṣṭo mahātmā pradadau varān lokapālopamān putrān ekaikasyā yathepsitān
english: Pleased with them, that blessed great-souled one granted boons to each of them — sons comparable to world-guardians, as each desired.

sanskrit: puṣpotkaṭāyāṃ jajñāte dvau putrau rākṣaseśvarau kumbhakarṇadaśagrīvau balenāpratimau bhuvi
english: In Puṣpotkaṭā were born two sons who became lords of rākṣasas — Kumbhakarṇa and Daśagrīva — matchless in strength on earth.

sanskrit: mālinī janayām āsa putram ekaṃ vibhīṣaṇam rākāyāṃ mithunaṃ jajñe kharaḥ śūrpaṇakhā tathā
english: Mālinī gave birth to one son, Vibhīṣaṇa; in Rākā were born twins — Khara and Śūrpaṇakhā.

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇas tu rūpeṇa sarvebhyo 'bhyadhiko 'bhavat sa babhūva mahābhāgo dharmagoptā kriyāratiḥ
english: Vibhīṣaṇa surpassed all others in beauty; he became greatly blessed, a guardian of dharma, devoted to righteous acts.

sanskrit: daśagrīvas tu sarveṣāṃ jyeṣṭho rākṣasapuṃgavaḥ mahotsāho mahāvīryo mahāsattvaparākramaḥ
english: Daśagrīva was the eldest of all, the foremost among rākṣasas, of great energy, great heroism, great strength and valour.

sanskrit: kumbhakarṇo balenāsīt sarvebhyo 'bhyadhikas tadā māyāvī raṇaśauṇḍaś ca raudraś ca rajanīcaraḥ
english: Kumbhakarṇa surpassed all others in physical strength at that time; he was a master of illusion, keen in battle, fierce, and a night-wanderer.

sanskrit: kharo dhanuṣi vikrānto brahmadviṭ piśitāśanaḥ siddhavighnakarī cāpi raudrā śūrpaṇakhā tathā
english: Khara was valiant with the bow, a hater of brāhmaṇas, a flesh-eater; and Śūrpaṇakhā too was fierce, one who creates obstacles for the virtuous.

sanskrit: sarve vedavidaḥ śūrāḥ sarve sucaritavratāḥ ūṣuḥ pitrā saha ratā gandhamādanaparvate
english: All of them were learned in the Vedas, all were heroes, all observed excellent vows; devoted to their father, they lived on Mount Gandhamādana.

sanskrit: tato vaiśravaṇaṃ tatra dadṛśur naravāhanam pitrā sārdhaṃ samāsīnam ṛddhyā paramayā yutam
english: Then there they saw Vaiśravaṇa, the bearer of human conveyance (Kubera), seated together with their father, endowed with supreme prosperity.

sanskrit: jātaspardhās tatas te tu tapase dhṛtaniścayāḥ brahmāṇaṃ toṣayām āsur ghoreṇa tapasā tadā
english: Rivalry having arisen in them, they resolved upon asceticism and pleased Brahmā with fierce austerities.

sanskrit: atiṣṭhad ekapādena sahasraṃ parivatsarān vāyubhakṣo daśagrīvaḥ pañcāgniḥ susamāhitaḥ
english: Daśagrīva stood on one foot for a thousand years, subsisting on air, practising the five-fire penance, perfectly concentrated.

sanskrit: adhaḥśāyī kumbhakarṇo yatāhāro yatavrataḥ vibhīṣaṇaḥ śīrṇaparṇam ekam abhyavahārayat
english: Kumbhakarṇa lay face-downward, disciplined in food and vows; Vibhīṣaṇa subsisted on a single fallen leaf.

sanskrit: upavāsaratir dhīmān sadā japyaparāyaṇaḥ tam eva kālam ātiṣṭhat tīvraṃ tapa udāradhīḥ
english: Devoted to fasting, wise, ever intent on recitation of mantras, that noble-minded one maintained that same intense austerity throughout the entire period.

sanskrit: kharaḥ śūrpaṇakhā caiva teṣāṃ vai tapyatāṃ tapaḥ paricaryāṃ ca rakṣāṃ ca cakratur hṛṣṭamānasau
english: Khara and Śūrpaṇakhā, with joyful hearts, attended upon and guarded the others as they performed their austerities.

sanskrit: pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu śiraś chittvā daśānanaḥ juhoty agnau durādharṣas tenātuṣyaj jagatprabhuḥ
english: When a thousand years were complete, the irresistible ten-headed one cut off his head and offered it in fire; by this the lord of the universe was pleased.

sanskrit: tato brahmā svayaṃ gatvā tapasas tān nyavārayat pralobhya varadānena sarvān eva pṛthak pṛthak
english: Then Brahmā himself went there, stopped them from their austerities, and enticed each of them separately with the granting of boons.

sanskrit: brahmovāca prīto 'smi vo nivartadhvaṃ varān vṛṇuta putrakāḥ yad yad iṣṭam ṛte tv ekam amaratvaṃ tathāstu tat
english: Brahmā said: I am pleased with you; desist, dear sons, and choose boons — whatever is desired, save one thing: immortality — let that be so.

sanskrit: yad yad agnau hutaṃ sarvaṃ śiras te mahad īpsayā tathaiva tāni te dehe bhaviṣyanti yathepsitam
english: "All those heads of yours that were offered in the fire with great desire — even so, all of them shall exist on your body as you wish."

sanskrit: vairūpyaṃ ca na te dehe kāmarūpadharas tathā bhaviṣyasi raṇe 'rīṇāṃ vijetāsi na saṃśayaḥ
english: "And your body shall bear no deformity; you will be able to assume any form at will, and you will be victorious over your enemies in battle — of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: rāvaṇa uvāca gandharvadevāsurato yakṣarākṣasatas tathā sarpakiṃnarabhūtebhyo na me bhūyāt parābhavaḥ
english: Rāvaṇa said: From gandharvas, gods, asuras, yakṣas, rākṣasas, serpents, kiṃnaras, and spirits — may I never suffer defeat.

sanskrit: brahmovāca ya ete kīrtitāḥ sarve na tebhyo 'sti bhayaṃ tava ṛte manuṣyād bhadraṃ te tathā tad vihitaṃ mayā
english: Brahmā said: From all those you have mentioned, there shall be no fear for you — except from a human. Be well; so has it been ordained by me.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca evam ukto daśagrīvas tuṣṭaḥ samabhavat tadā avamene hi durbuddhir manuṣyān puruṣādakaḥ
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Thus addressed, Daśagrīva became satisfied at that time; for that evil-minded man-eater despised human beings.

sanskrit: kumbhakarṇam athovāca tathaiva prapitāmahaḥ sa vavre mahatīṃ nidrāṃ tamasā grastacetanaḥ
english: Then the great-grandfather spoke similarly to Kumbhakarṇa; but his mind being seized by delusion, he chose great sleep.

sanskrit: tathā bhaviṣyatīty uktvā vibhīṣaṇam uvāca ha varaṃ vṛṇīṣva putra tvaṃ prīto 'smīti punaḥ punaḥ
english: Saying "So shall it be," he then spoke to Vibhīṣaṇa: "Choose a boon, my son" — repeatedly saying "I am pleased with you."

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇa uvāca paramāpadgatasyāpi nādharme me matir bhavet aśikṣitaṃ ca bhagavan brahmāstraṃ pratibhātu me
english: Vibhīṣaṇa said: Even when fallen into the greatest adversity, may my mind never turn to adharma; and O blessed one, may the Brahmāstra manifest to me though untaught.

sanskrit: brahmovāca yasmād rākṣasayonau te jātasyāmitrakarśana nādharme ramate buddhir amaratvaṃ dadāmi te
english: Brahmā said: Because, though born in the rākṣasa womb, O scorcher of foes, your mind takes no pleasure in adharma — I grant you immortality.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca rākṣasas tu varaṃ labdhvā daśagrīvo viśāṃ pate laṅkāyāś cyāvayām āsa yudhi jitvā dhaneśvaram
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Having obtained the boon, O lord of men, Daśagrīva the rākṣasa expelled the lord of wealth from Laṅkā after defeating him in battle.

sanskrit: hitvā sa bhagavāṃl laṅkām āviśad gandhamādanam gandharvayakṣānugato rakṣaḥkiṃpuruṣaiḥ saha
english: The blessed Kubera abandoned Laṅkā and retired to Gandhamādana, accompanied by gandharvas and yakṣas along with rākṣasas and kiṃpuruṣas.

sanskrit: vimānaṃ puṣpakaṃ tasya jahārākramya rāvaṇaḥ śaśāpa taṃ vaiśravaṇo na tvām etad vahiṣyati
english: Rāvaṇa seized and carried off his aerial chariot Puṣpaka; Vaiśravaṇa cursed him: "This shall no longer carry you."

sanskrit: yas tu tvāṃ samare hantā tam evaitad vahiṣyati avamanya guruṃ māṃ ca kṣipraṃ tvaṃ na bhaviṣyasi
english: "This shall carry him who kills you in battle; having dishonoured your elder and me, you shall swiftly cease to be."

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇas tu dharmātmā satāṃ dharmam anusmaran anvagacchan mahārāja śriyā paramayā yutaḥ
english: But Vibhīṣaṇa, righteous in soul, ever mindful of the dharma of the virtuous, followed Kubera, O great king, endowed with supreme prosperity.

sanskrit: tasmai sa bhagavāṃs tuṣṭo bhrātā bhrātre dhaneśvaraḥ senāpatyaṃ dadau dhīmān yakṣarākṣasasenayoḥ
english: Pleased with him, that blessed lord of wealth, the wise brother, gave his brother the commandership of both the yakṣa and rākṣasa armies.

sanskrit: rākṣasāḥ puruṣādāś ca piśācāś ca mahābalāḥ sarve sametya rājānam abhyaṣiñcad daśānanam
english: The rākṣasas, man-eaters, and the mighty piśācas — all assembled and consecrated Daśānana as king.

sanskrit: daśagrīvas tu daityānāṃ devānāṃ ca balotkaṭaḥ ākramya ratnāny aharat kāmarūpī vihaṃgamaḥ
english: Daśagrīva, excelling in power over daityas and gods alike, moving through the sky and assuming any form at will, seized and carried off their treasures.

sanskrit: rāvayām āsa lokān yat tasmād rāvaṇa ucyate daśagrīvaḥ kāmabalo devānāṃ bhayam ādadhat
english: Because he made the worlds cry out in terror, Daśagrīva is therefore called Rāvaṇa; powerful as he willed, he instilled fear in the gods.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tato brahmarṣayaḥ siddhā devarājarṣayas tathā havyavāhaṃ puraskṛtya brahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Then the brahmarṣis, the siddhas, and the divine royal sages, placing Agni (the fire-carrier) before them, sought refuge with Brahmā.

sanskrit: agnir uvāca yaḥ sa viśravasaḥ putro daśagrīvo mahābalaḥ avadhyo varadānena kṛto bhagavatā purā
english: Agni said: That son of Viśravā, Daśagrīva the mighty, has been made unkillable in times past by the blessed one's boon.

sanskrit: sa bādhate prajāḥ sarvā viprakārair mahābalaḥ tato nas trātu bhagavan nānyas trātā hi vidyate
english: The mighty one oppresses all creatures with his outrages; therefore, O blessed one, protect us — for no other protector exists.

sanskrit: brahmovāca na sa devāsuraiḥ śakyo yuddhe jetuṃ vibhāvaso vihitaṃ tatra yat kāryam abhitas tasya nigrahe
english: Brahmā said: O Fire, he cannot be conquered in battle by gods or asuras; yet what needs to be done for his destruction has been arranged all around.

sanskrit: tadartham avatīrṇo 'sau manniyogāc caturbhujaḥ viṣṇuḥ praharatāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ sa karmaitat kariṣyati
english: "For this very purpose, the four-armed Viṣṇu, the foremost among those who strike, has descended at my command; he shall accomplish this deed."

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca pitāmahas tatas teṣāṃ saṃnidhau vākyam abravīt sarvair devagaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃbhavadhvaṃ mahītale
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: The Grandfather then spoke this word in the presence of all those assembled, together with all the hosts of gods: "Be born on the earth."

sanskrit: viṣṇoḥ sahāyān ṛkṣīṣu vānarīṣu ca sarvaśaḥ janayadhvaṃ sutān vīrān kāmarūpabalānvitān
english: "Beget valiant sons as helpers of Viṣṇu, everywhere among the she-bears and female monkeys — sons endowed with strength and the power to assume any form."
